chunks: And with this chain of transmission, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abi Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a large jar in which wine had been kept: is it suitable for vinegar, or kamikh water, or olives to be placed in it? He said: “If it is washed, then there is no harm.” And about a ewer in which there is wine: is it suitable for water to be in it? He said: “If it is washed, then there is no harm.” And he said regarding a cup or vessel from which wine is drunk: “Wash it three times.” He was asked: would it suffice for him to pour water into it? He said: “It does not suffice until he scrubs it with his hand and washes it three times.”

key_terms.الدَّنِّ: a large storage jar or cask
key_terms.الْخَلُّ: vinegar intended to be placed in the vessel after purification
key_terms.الْخَمْرُ: wine, treated here as a najis substance requiring purification of the vessel
key_terms.ثَلَاثَ مَرَّاتٍ: three times, the specified number of washes required here
key_terms.غُسِلَ: was washed, meaning ritually cleaned for reuse

ai.seo_question: How should a vessel that contained wine be purified before it can be used again?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on purifying vessels that had contained or been used for wine. It states that such containers may be used again after washing, and in the case of a cup or vessel used for drinking wine, it must be scrubbed and washed three times.
